route: oral, PFOS-contaminated grass pellets from a river floodplain, up to 112 d, with a subgroup switched to clean grass after 56 d
parameter: retained fraction (% of PFOS ingested from grass present in liver)

dose_linearity: single contaminated-feed level
source_table: Abstract (liver retention percentages and liver concentration time course)
notes: Abstract retrieved via NCBI efetch (Elsevier Chemosphere full text not open). Liver PFOS rose from 2.4 to 10.9 ng/g ww between day 8 and day 112 of exposure; in the depuration subgroup it fell from 9.2 to 4.7 ng/g ww between day 64 and day 112 (i.e. 8 and 56 d after switching to clean grass). EFSA reports no half-life for these compounds in mice ('NR'), only total clearance and, for the i.v. route, volume of distribution. Gastrointestinal absorption of the C11-C14 PFCAs was at or near 100% in both sexes. SEX-LABEL CAVEAT: EFSA Table C.3 labels the two mouse columns 'Mice (F)' then 'Mice (M)', but the accompanying Appendix C.1 narrative states the i.v. distribution volumes 'varied from 280 to 430 mL/kg in males and from 330 to 580 mL/kg in females', which matches the columns in the OPPOSITE order. The sex assignment of the two columns is therefore internally inconsistent in the EFSA Opinion; the table's own labels are used here and the conflict is flagged.
